fields.h1: Build Sales Automation for Every Lead, Deal and Renewal
fields.hero_description: Build sales automation that assigns new leads by territory and messages the owner in Slack when a deal stalls, beside your CRM.
fields.features_heading: What Sales Automation Handles for Reps
fields.features_subheading: Sales automation hands the repeat steps of a deal to software. Below are six parts of that job, each running as code your team owns.
fields.feature_1:
Every new lead assigned on arrival

Demo requests, chat leads and event scans land in one table. Each new lead goes to a rep by territory or by round-robin rotation. The queue shows whose turn is next.
fields.feature_2:
Reps send sequences from their own inbox

Emails go out from the rep's Gmail or Outlook, in their name, on the days the team picks. Reps can see which step each prospect has reached before they pick up the phone.
fields.feature_3:
CRM records that update themselves

Sent emails and meeting notes sync to Salesforce or HubSpot through their APIs. Each contact record shows its latest touch without a rep typing it in on Friday afternoon.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts on deals that slip

A close date pushed twice, or a proposal with no answer after 7 days, sends the owner a Slack message. It comes back each morning until someone moves the deal forward.
fields.feature_5:
Discount approvals in Slack

A discount above the threshold goes to a sales manager in Slack. The request shows deal size and margin. Each decision is logged on the deal under the approver's name.
fields.feature_6:
Territory rules stored as readable code

Routing tables, cadences and the dashboard export to GitHub as code on paid plans. When a rep leaves, moving their accounts to a new owner is a prompt or a pull request.

fields.tab_content_1:
New demo requests go to the right rep while they are warm

A demo request from an existing HubSpot account goes to its owner. New companies are enriched with size and region. Companies with 200 or more employees go to the enterprise rep for their region, and the rest rotate across the team. HubSpot records the new owner, then the rep gets a direct message in Slack.
fields.tab_content_2:
Post-demo follow-up stops the moment a buyer replies

The recap leaves the rep's inbox on the day of the demo, and a second email follows on day 3. With no reply by day 7, the rep gets a call task as a Slack direct message. Any reply or booked meeting ends the sequence and is logged on the deal.
fields.tab_content_3:
Quiet deals surface before Friday's forecast call

Every morning, each open deal is checked for days since its last logged activity. A deal with no touch in 14 days is marked on the pipeline dashboard. Its owner gets a Slack direct message with the deal value and the last email sent. The flag clears once the owner logs a call or books the next meeting.
fields.tab_content_4:
When a contract is 90 days from ending, renewal work starts

Contract end dates are read from HubSpot each Monday. An account that crossed into the 90-day window since the last run gets one renewal deal, owned by its account manager. That manager gets a Slack direct message listing each account in the window with its price and open support tickets.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn your routing and follow-up rules into sales automation, then roll it out one lead source at a time.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Map how a lead becomes a customer
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write routing rules in plain English
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every source that sends you leads, with the demo form at the top. Note who owns each stage and where deals tend to wait. That map becomes the pipeline stages Emergent builds and the routing that feeds them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe assignment the way your sales ops lead would explain it to a new hire. Partner referrals go to the partner manager; healthcare leads go to the rep who covers clinics. Emergent turns those sentences into rules you can read and change later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what happens when a prospect misses a booked demo or goes silent after a proposal. Pick the days each email goes out and the point where a phone call replaces email. Write the templates in your reps' own voice.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the CRM your team works in, plus the Gmail or Outlook accounts reps send from. Start with one rep's inbox and one pipeline, then add the rest. Managers keep reporting from the CRM they already use.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the few signals worth interrupting a rep for, such as a renewal account with an urgent support ticket open, or a new lead from a company already deep in a deal. Decide who hears first. The owner gets the message; their manager is copied when 2 days pass with no update.
fields.howto_step_6_des: For 1 week, the app suggests an owner for each new lead while reps keep assigning by hand. Compare its picks with theirs at the end of each day. Where the two differ, fix the rule by prompting before routing goes live.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Switch on one lead source first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn routing on for the demo form and add chat leads 1 week later. Watch time to first touch on the dashboard. When that number drifts, change the rule behind it with a prompt. Bring in outbound lists last.

Outreach is a sales engagement platform whose sequences combine automatic emails with phone call steps

Flagging deals with no logged activity in 14 days is a common pipeline-hygiene rule
Renewal work commonly starts 90 days or more before a contract ends
Sales CRMs and engagement platforms price per user or seat per month, with automation in higher editions
Salesforce Sales Cloud and HubSpot Sales Hub both include workflow automation

An automated sales funnel is the path from first contact to closed deal, with software moving the prospect through each stage
